rationale: Sources 2 (coddy.tech) and 4 (sqlfmt.app) independently confirm that SQLite WAL mode allows concurrent readers and writers without blocking one another, whereas source 1 truncates before answering and source 3 describes rollback-journal locking.
Sources 1/4 (IETF/RFC Editor, counted once), 2 (xgm.ro), and 3 (sslinsights.com) corroborate that RFC 8996 deprecates TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and RFC 8446 eliminates legacy cipher suites in TLS 1.3.

All four independent clinical publishers (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) consistently state that aspirin is contraindicated in children and teenagers with viral illnesses such as influenza or varicella due to Reye syndrome risk.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) identify Uji in Kyoto Prefecture as the renowned Japanese region for Uji matcha cultivation.

None of the retrieved sources (1-4) include the actual Fahrenheit cooking temperature for poultry in their snippets or previews, as source 2 truncates right at 'Cook all poultry ...' and sources 1, 3, and 4 show only introductory boilerplate.

Source 2 (Cochrane) explicitly concludes there is no evidence supporting ivermectin for treating COVID-19 and source 1 (PMC) notes WHO recommends against use outside clinical trials while explicitly documenting controversy in the literature.
Sources 1, 2, 3, and 4 (capped at 3) agree that briefly rinsing mushrooms right before cooking does not ruin or waterlog them, while explicitly debunking the widespread kitchen myth in the query.
Sources 2, 3, and 4 report Mount Rainier's elevation as 14,410 ft (4,392 m), materially conflicting with source 1 (Wikipedia), which states 14,406 ft (4,391 m).

All four independent medical sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) consistently explain that honey can contain Clostridium bacteria spores that cause life-threatening infant botulism in babies under 12 months.

Only source 4 (ThoughtCo) addresses the query—explaining that salt slightly raises water's boiling point by an unnoticeable amount—whereas sources 1, 2, and 3 are off-topic articles about drinking salt water for hydration.
Only source 2 (Server Fault) mentions the 512-byte UDP size limit for DNS, while sources 1, 3, and 4 discuss generic UDP headers or IP MTU limits without addressing DNS or RFC 1035.

Sources 1, 2, 3, and 4 (capped at 3) all address the active scientific debate over the relative causal roles and coincident timing of the Chicxulub impact and Deccan Traps volcanism in the end-Cretaceous extinction.

Sources 1 (Wikipedia) and 4 (MedlinePlus aggregated snippet) explicitly identify toxic chlorine gas as released when bleach is mixed with acids, whereas sources 2 and 3 mention generic irritant/toxic gases without naming chlorine.
None of the retrieved sources (1-4) mention anaphylaxis or epinephrine, as all four are general nursing tutorials on generic intramuscular injection procedures.

Only source 2 (Stack Overflow) substantively explains that git fetch updates remote-tracking refs without altering local branches while git pull performs a fetch followed by a merge; sources 1, 3, and 4 contain only headers or partial git-fetch boilerplate.

Sources 1, 2, and 4 (with source 3 also clarifying Faenza's Italian origin) consistently document that majolica derives from Italian Renaissance tin-glazed earthenware (maiolica) centered in towns like Faenza, Deruta, Gubbio, and Urbino.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm that a standard English Scrabble set has 100 tiles consisting of 98 letter tiles and 2 blank tiles.
Sources 2, 3, and 4 (along with source 1) independently confirm that enabling TCP_NODELAY disables Nagle's packet-buffering algorithm on TCP sockets.

Sources 2 (webassembly.github.io snippet) and 3 (MDN) confirm that WebAssembly linear memory is raw byte-addressed in little-endian format, whereas sources 1 and 4 contain only high-level introductory sections.
Only source 4 (portchecker.cc) specifies port 123 (for UDP) for NTP, while sources 1, 2, and 3 contain no port number assignments in their retrieved text.

None of the retrieved pages (all from en.wikipedia.org) address sugar maple autumn leaf pigments; sources 1, 3, and 4 are off-topic and source 2 mentions carotenoids in 15-30% of trees generally without mentioning sugar maples or anthocyanins.

Sources 2 (PubMed/NCBI) and 4 (Dr.Oracle) indicate moderate coffee consumption reduces or does not trigger atrial fibrillation/arrhythmias, conflicting with source 1 (PMC/NCBI), which cites studies associating caffeine with cardiac arrhythmias.

Sources 1 (Fire Engineering) and 4 (NASP) substantively explain that lithium-ion thermal runaway drives a chemical chain reaction producing extreme heat, flammable gases, toxic smoke, and explosions, whereas source 2 gives only a general overview and source 3 is an error page.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm that rosin (hardened pine resin) is rubbed onto violin bow horsehair to grip the strings and create friction.

Sources 1 (Meilleur du Chef) and 3 (CakeDecoratingCalc) provide complete, consistent three-stage dark couverture tempering ranges (45-50°C/115-120°F melt, ~28°C/82-84°F cool, 31-32°C/88-90°F work), while source 2 lacks numbers and source 4 truncates after melting.
Sources 1 (Wikipedia), 2 (MLB.com), and 3 (SportsMonkie) independently confirm that a sacrifice fly does not count as an official time at bat or reduce batting average.
The sole retrieved source (source 1, Wikipedia's Tea culture article) discusses Darjeeling tea and general tea drinking without mentioning Earl Grey or bergamot oil.

Sources 1, 2, and 4 discuss competing methodological/calibration and ΛCDM cosmological-parameter explanations for the actively disputed Hubble constant discrepancy between CMB and local distance-ladder measurements.

Only source 3 (chess.phd) states all five castling rules and distinguishes the two permanent king/rook-movement conditions from the three temporary occupied/attacked-square conditions, whereas sources 1, 2, and 4 truncate before explaining them.
Only source 4 (sharpskill.dev) explicitly states that Rust allows only one exclusive mutable reference at a time, while sources 1, 2, and 3 do not state the concurrency rule in their retrieved text.

Sources 1 (OWASP), 3 (Encryption Consulting), and 4 (wtool.dev), corroborated by source 2, confirm that OWASP recommends Argon2id because salted, slow, memory-hard hashing resists GPU brute-force and precomputed rainbow-table attacks.
Sources 2 (BBC Sky at Night), 3 (FactSentinel), and 4 (PMC) independently confirm the Great Wall is not visible to the unaided eye from orbit and explicitly refute the widespread popular myth.

All four retrieved URLs belong to wikipedia.org (counting as 1 source total) and identify J. S. Bach, while source 3 (es.wikipedia, 1742) and source 4 (de.wikipedia, 1741) contradict one another on the first publication year.

Sources 1/2 (both nist.gov, counted once) and 3 (safeguard.sh) explain that NIST deprecated and disallowed SHA-1 for signatures due to collision/attacker-chosen-input vulnerabilities, whereas source 4 states only retirement dates.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm that epoll replaced select and poll in the Linux kernel for scalable O(1) I/O event readiness notification.

Sources 1 (Medscape) and 4 (Drugs.com) explicitly identify N-acetylcysteine (acetylcysteine/NAC) as the antidote for acute acetaminophen poisoning, whereas source 2 shows only table-of-contents headings and source 3 is blocked.

Only source 3 (FactGuard) addresses taste zones—confirming all taste receptors exist across the entire tongue and explicitly debunking the widespread 'tongue map' myth—while sources 1, 2, and 4 cover unrelated anatomy or tongue splitting.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) state the exact vacuum speed of light as 299,792,458 meters per second defining the SI meter.

Sources 1, 2, and 4 reprint the verbatim statutory text of GDPR Article 33(1) (counted as 1 source total) and source 3 (Recording Law) independently corroborates the 72-hour supervisory authority notification requirement.

Only source 2 (Unseel) states the 273.16 K triple-point temperature for Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water, whereas sources 1, 3, and 4 omit the Kelvin value for the triple point in their retrieved previews.

Sources 1 (Engineers Universe) and 4 (Schneider Electric) explain that NEC GFCI rules protect against shock and electrocution by tripping rapidly on current imbalance/leakage to ground, while sources 2 and 3 lack substantive explanation.
Sources 1 (Wikipedia), 2 (GeeksforGeeks), and 3 (University of Iowa) independently confirm that IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long compared with 32 bits for IPv4.

All four independent medical and regulatory sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm the standard 4,000 mg 24-hour adult maximum ceiling for acetaminophen to prevent liver toxicity (with complementary lower OTC precautions noted).

Sources 1 (Verywell Health), 2 (Biology Insights), and 4 (WebMD) report insufficient or low-quality clinical evidence for Oscillococcinum in flu treatment, contradicting manufacturer source 3 (Oscillo.com), which claims clinical efficacy.

Sources 1, 2, and 4 confirm Napoleon stood roughly 5'6" to 5'7"—average or slightly above average for French men of his era—while explicitly debunking the shortness myth and noting historical disagreement.
Sources 2 (binarycon.com) and 3 (ElectricalFlux) specify the IEEE 754 binary64 allocation of 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, and 52 fraction/mantissa bits, while sources 1 and 4 omit the bit counts.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm that gluten (formed from glutenin and gliadin proteins) creates the elastic network in kneaded bread dough.

Only source 4 (martinuke0.github.io) contrasts both levels—explaining that READ COMMITTED takes a fresh snapshot per statement while REPEATABLE READ fixes the snapshot for the entire transaction—whereas source 1 covers only Repeatable Read and sources 2-3 show outlines.

Only source 4 (ScienceDaily) addresses cold prevention—reporting that larger studies show vitamin C does not prevent colds in most people and refuting popular Pauling/marketing claims—while sources 1-3 only discuss toxicity or are blocked.
Sources 1 (RFC Editor), 3 (MDN), and 4 (Microsoft Learn) confirm HTTP status code 429 Too Many Requests for rate limiting (standardized in RFC 6585), whereas source 2 shows only RFC boilerplate.
All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm the official standardized marathon distance is 42.195 kilometers.
Sources 1, 3, and 4 identify Akira Kurosawa as director of Seven Samurai (studio omitted in previews), but all four URLs belong to en.wikipedia.org and therefore count as 1 source total.

Sources 2 (CDC) and 4 (Trail Manual) explain that portable gasoline engines emit colorless, odorless carbon monoxide that rapidly reaches lethal levels in enclosed garages and blocks blood oxygen transport via high-affinity hemoglobin binding.

All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) report consistent physical carbon-14 half-life values of 5,700 ± 30 years / 5,730 years (overlapping within the stated 30-year uncertainty).

None of the retrieved sources (1-4) identify the wood species (spruce) used for classical concert harp soundboards or violin tops; sources 1-3 have no species names and source 4 discusses guitar woods.

All four independent sources (sources 1, 2, 3, and 4, capped at 3) confirm the IAU reclassified Pluto in 2006 over the 'cleared the neighborhood' criterion and document ongoing disagreement among planetary astronomers.
Sources 1/2 (both wikipedia.org, counted once), 3 (The Fact Site), and 4 (SettlersBoard) independently confirm Klaus Teuber's Settlers of Catan was first published in Germany in 1995.

Sources 1, 2, and 3 substantively describe the active scientific dispute over whether Venus's candidate spectral line is genuine phosphine, instrumental/molecular systematics, and unexplained abiotic vs biological origins.

Only source 1 (PMC) notes that combining an MAOI with a serotonergic psychiatric medication risks serotonin syndrome, whereas source 2 covers stimulants, source 3 lacks interaction details on the same NCBI domain, and source 4 mentions only tyramine/blood pressure.

Sources 2, 3, and 4 all reproduce or log the exact same IETF RFC 9114 abstract naming QUIC (counting as 1 source total under same-org and verbatim-copy rules), while source 1 truncates before naming QUIC.
None of the retrieved sources (1-4) state how many feathers are in a shuttlecock, discussing only goose vs duck feather quality and wing symmetry.

None of the retrieved previews (1-4) mention simvastatin or lovastatin or link them to a specific clinical interaction, as source 2 stops at general CYP3A4 metabolism and source 3 lists broad cross-drug side effects without reaching L or S drugs.
Only source 1 (Wikipedia) states that modern pianos have 88 keys, whereas sources 2, 3, and 4 are off-topic pages about Grand Concert acoustic guitars.

Sources 1, 2, and 3 all belong to python.org (counting as 1 source total, specifying October 7, 2024 and PEP 703), while source 4 omits PEP 703 and only reprints Python.org's verbatim release snippet for the date.
